title: Unitary Bessel models and the Gan–Gross–Prasad period formula
summary: Construct the relative unitary Bessel library in every relevant odd codimension, prove characteristic-zero local multiplicity one and the tempered nonsplit packet character theorem, formulate the general global conjecture, and prove adjacent global nonvanishing and GGP.8 with completed factors and Tamagawa measures. Explicit gaps delimit unavailable general suppliers.

layers.title: Relative Hermitian geometry and Bessel data

targets.name: RelevantHermitianPair
targets.statement: For the algebraic hypotheses below, define RelevantHermitianPair(W,V,r,L) to mean an isometric inclusion i:W→V together with the property that i(W)⊥ is isometric to H^r orthogonal-sum L, where H has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,0]] and L=<a> with a∈F×. A framed pair additionally chooses such an isometry, a hyperbolic basis and an E-basis vector e of L, meaning E→L, a↦ae is an isomorphism (equivalently h(e,e)∈F×); relevance itself forgets the frame.
hypotheses: F is a field of characteristic different from 2
E is a quadratic étale F-algebra with its nontrivial involution c
All Hermitian E-modules are finite free of constant rank and their forms are nondegenerate
n=rank_E W, r≥0 and L is a nondegenerate rank-one space

targets.name: besselTransport
targets.statement: An isometry of framed pairs induces an isomorphism of the embedded (H,ν) data. Changing flag, hyperbolic frame, line generator or generic additive data on a fixed pair gives a conjugate embedded model, with the induced intertwining maps on Hom spaces. Simultaneous scaling h_V,h_W by a∈F× preserves the underlying unitary groups and transports the relative data; over R, a=-1 exchanges the two line signs. The transports respect identity and composition.

targets.name: besselModel
targets.statement: For local data of 1.2 define besselModel(π_V,π_W) as Hom_H(π_V|H tensor π_W|H,ν). At finite places this is the subspace of algebraic linear functionals satisfying ℓ(π_V(u i(g))v tensor π_W(g)w)=ν(u,g)ℓ(v tensor w). At infinity use continuous linear functionals on the completed projective tensor product. Define besselMultiplicity as its complex vector-space dimension, initially a cardinal; finite-dimensionality precedes its natural-number form.

targets.name: adjacentInvariantDistribution_symmetry

targets.name: ggpEpsilonCharacter
targets.statement: For the stated tempered parameter data construct χ=(χ_W,χ_V):A_(φ_V)×A_(φ_W)→{±1}. If s is represented by an involution in the parameter centralizer, set χ_W(s)=ε(1/2,φ_V^(s=-1) tensor φ_W,ψ_E), and interchange V,W for χ_V. Prove independence of lift and conjugate-dual form and the character law. On the generator for a distinct appropriate-sign irreducible ρ this is ε(1/2,ρ tensor φ_W,ψ_E), with one copy of ρ, not its full multiplicity. The central element z_φ is the image of -Id and includes the multiplicities modulo two.

The two generator values are ε(χ₁,ψ_E), ε(χ₋₁,ψ_E), and their product is χ₁(-1)=-1 by epsilon duality. Hence ggpEpsilonCharacter gives χ_W(z_(φ_V))=-1; the constant character fails (ggp §5, p. 16, line 598–601).

Then ggpEpsilonCharacter has value -1 on the single component generator but +1 on z_(φ_V)=0, whose multiplicity is even. Using the whole multiplicity at the generator would wrongly give +1 (ggp §5, p. 16, line 598–601; Theorem 6.1, p. 20).

Under the corresponding change of Whittaker datum the actual packet labeling changes by exactly these characters; simultaneous scaling of the two Hermitian forms and transport of their Whittaker data gives the same represented Bessel pair under 1.3.

targets.name: besselGeometricMultiplicity
targets.statement: For a relevant nonsplit local pair define Γ(G,H) to be the semisimple U(W)-conjugacy classes x for which U(im(x-1))_x is an anisotropic torus. Write W=ker(x-1) orthogonal-sum im(x-1). Give Γ the torus quotient measure with each anisotropic torus of mass 1 and rational Weyl-group divisor. Set D_G(x)=|det(1-Ad(x) on g/g_x)|, D_H analogously and Δ=D_G D_H⁻². For a Harish–Chandra quasi-character θ, put c_θ(x)=0 if the regular-nilpotent orbit set in g_x is empty; otherwise let c_θ(x) be the average of its finitely many germ coefficients, normalized by the supplied Fourier orbital measures. Define m_geom(θ)=lim_(s→0+) ∫_Γ D_G(x)^(1/2)c_θ(x)Δ(x)^(s-1/2) dx. Prove convergence for Re(s)>0, existence of the limit, continuity, semisimple descent, and compatibility with normalized parabolic induction.
